(U//FOUO) Travel Records Regarding Jeffrey Epstein, Main Subject in a
Child Sex 'frafficking Investigation, Establishes Travel Pattern to Posture for
an Arrest

(U) Executive Summary

(W/FOUO) FBI New York C-20 is investigating Jeffry Epstein as a main subject in child sex
trafficking investigation based on information regarding several victims reportedly sexually
abused by Epstein in the mid-2000s. Epstein owned four residences located in New York,
Florida, the Virgin Islands, and New Mexico and was known to travel extensively via his own
private accommodations. FBI New York conducted extensive research on Epstein's travel
history in order to establish a pattern for his arrest.

    •   (U/fFOUO) Epstein commonly used Teterboro, New Jersey International Airport for
        INBOUND flights from various locations
    •   (U//FOUO) Paris, France identified as Epstein's frequented travel destination secondary
        to where he resides
    •   (U/fFOUO) Epstein maintains three United States Passports, but only one remains active
    •   (U/fFOUO) Epstein owned and traveled on private aircrafts

(U) This TIR addresses FBI New York Criminal Division Band II Threat — Crimes Against
Children.

(U) Substantiation

(U//FOUO) Travel records reviewed for Jeffrey Epstein between 1 July 2017 to 14 June 2019
revealed travel patterns identified below, which assisted in forecasting Epstein's return to the
United States and subsequent arrest. As a result, Epstein was arrested on 6 July 2019 after
returning to the United States on his private plane at Teterboro, New Jersey from Paris, France.
